questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense. There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

• Tense remains same

• Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

• Past perfect changes to Simple Past

Case 2 is applicable in this question.

Case 2: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'Mentioned' is changed into 'said'.

'He had' is changed into 'I have'.

'His' is changed into 'my'.

Also, inverted commas ("..") are placed in direct speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is: My cousin said, "I have successfully completed my advanced certification course in digital marketing from a very renowned international university."

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.questionHtml: In the sentence, "Oysters are highly perishable and need to be kept cold and alive right up until they hit your plate," what is the grammatical function of the phrase "to be kept cold and alive right up until they hit your plate"?

options.text: Infinitive phrase expressing necessity or requirement
options.html: Infinitive phrase expressing necessity or requirement

questions.solution:
The phrase begins with "to be kept", forming an infinitive phrase that expresses a requirement for oysters due to their perishability. It explains what needs to happen to them, not indicating a condition, modifying "plate" or acting as an object. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

a) Adverbial phrase indicating a condition - Incorrect

The phrase does not state a condition (e.g., "if..., unless...").

Instead, it states what is required for oysters - not the circumstances under which something happens.

c) Object of the verb "hit" - Incorrect

The verb "hit" already has its object: "your plate"

The infinitive phrase is not receiving the action of "hit"; rather, it contains its own clause ("they hit your plate") inside it.

d) Adjective phrase modifying "plate" - Incorrect

The phrase does not describe "plate."

It describes what oysters need (a condition they must be kept in), not a quality of the plate.

Note:

Adverbial Phrase

A group of words that functions as an adverb, modifying a verb, adjective, or another adverb by answering how, when, where, why, or to what extent. It often includes prepositions or adverbs. Example: She sings with great passion. (With great passion explains how she sings.)

Infinitive Phrase

A phrase starting with an infinitive (to + base verb) and including modifiers or objects, acting as a noun, adjective, or adverb to express purpose, necessity, or description. Example: To learn coding quickly takes dedication. (To learn coding quickly acts as the subject.)

Adjective Phrase

A group of words that functions as an adjective, modifying a noun or pronoun by describing its qualities, quantity, or extent. It often centres on an adjective with modifiers. Example: The book full of adventure stories is on the shelf. (Full of adventure stories modifies book.)

questions.question: Rearrange the following steps of the geological formation of coal in the correct order: P. Over millions of years, intense heat and pressure transform the buried matter into coal. questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following steps of the geological formation of coal in the correct order:

P. Over millions of years, intense heat and pressure transform the buried matter into coal.

Q. Vast amounts of dead plant life accumulated in ancient, oxygen-poor swamp environments.

R. This organic material was buried by layers of sediment, forming a dense, soft substance called peat.

S. The quality of coal deepens from lignite to anthracite as the pressure and heat increase.
questions.solution:
The sequence describes the long geological process of coalification.

Q is the starting point: the accumulation of the raw organic material.

R is the next step, where this material is buried and undergoes the first stage of transformation into peat.

P describes the long-term geological process that acts upon the buried peat.

S provides further detail on the process described in P, explaining the different grades of coal that are formed.

Thus, the correct geological order is Q → R → P → S.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb ['is' here] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V1/V5 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

She likes you. (Active Voice)

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

(4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The new wellness program encourages employees to focus on their health (1)/ by eating more nutritious meals, exercising regularly, (2)/ and to get at least eight hours of sleep each night, (3)/ promoting a better work-life balance. (4)

options.text: The new wellness program encourages employees to focus on their health (1)
options.html: The new wellness program encourages employees to focus on their health (1)

options.text: and to get at least eight hours of sleep each night, (3)
options.html: and to get at least eight hours of sleep each night, (3)

options.text: by eating more nutritious meals, exercising regularly, (2)
options.html: by eating more nutritious meals, exercising regularly, (2)

questions.solution:
The error in part (3) is a violation of parallel structure. The sentence creates a list of ways employees can focus on their health, introduced by the preposition "by." All items in a list should have the same grammatical form. The preposition "by" should be followed either by a noun or a noun phrase, or a noun equivalent (gerund).

The first item is a gerund phrase: "eating more nutritious meals"

The second item is a gerund phrase: "exercising regularly"

The third item breaks the pattern by using an infinitive phrase: "to get at least eight hours of sleep".

To correct the sentence, the third item should also be a gerund phrase to match the others. That gerund phrase should begin with "getting..".

The corrected sentence should read: "The new wellness program encourages employees to focus on their health by eating more nutritious meals, exercising regularly, and getting at least eight hours of sleep each night, promoting a better work-life balance."

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note: Parallelism: In grammar, parallelism, also known as parallel structure or parallel construction, is a balance within one or more sentences of similar phrases or clauses that have the same grammatical structure. Given below is an example which shows a sentence in two forms (parallel in structure and lacking parallelism): Lacking parallelism: Prerna likes cooking, dancing and to sing. Parallel: Prerna likes cooking, dancing and singing.

Gerund: A Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or the object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [The infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [The infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

A relative clause is a dependent clause that begins with a relative pronoun (such as who, which, or that) or a relative adverb (where, when, or why), and it provides additional information about a noun.

Note:

Relative Clause: A relative clause is one that's connected to the main clause of the sentence by a word such as who, whom, which, that, or whose.

Example: He adopted a puppy that had brown eyes and black fur. The highlighted part is the relative clause.

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example, she is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

A participial phrase consists of a participle (a verb form used as an adjective) along with its modifiers, objects, and complements. The participle can be in the present form (ending in -ing) or the past form (usually ending in -ed, -en, or other irregular forms). For example:

Ribosomes are the molecular machines within a cell that are responsible for protein synthesis, a process also known as translation. They read the sequence of messenger RNA (mRNA), which carries the genetic code from the DNA, and use this code to link amino acids together in the correct order to form a polypeptide chain, which then folds into a functional protein.

It does not synthesize proteins.

Lysosome: Lysosomes are organelles that contain digestive enzymes. They function as the cell's waste disposal and recycling system, breaking down old cell parts, foreign material, and waste products.

Centriole: Centrioles are cylindrical structures that play a critical role in cell division (mitosis and meiosis) by helping to organize the mitotic spindle, which separates the chromosomes.

Further Insights:

In eukaryotic cells, ribosomes can be found in two locations: floating freely in the cytoplasm (where they synthesize proteins for use within the cell) and attached to the membrane of the rough endoplasmic reticulum (where they synthesize proteins destined for export from the cell or for insertion into membranes).

The process of protein synthesis is a central part of the "central dogma" of molecular biology: DNA is transcribed into RNA, and RNA is translated into protein.

Pioneer species are hardy organisms that are the first to colonize barren environments or previously biodiverse ecosystems that have been disrupted (e.g., by a fire, volcanic eruption, or landslide).

They are the initial stage of a process called ecological succession.

These species are typically characterized by their ability to tolerate harsh conditions, grow quickly, and reproduce rapidly.

Other options

(a) Indicator species: These are species whose presence, absence, or abundance reflects a specific environmental condition. For example, the presence of certain lichens can indicate good air quality. They signal the health of an ecosystem but are not necessarily the first to arrive.

(b) Keystone species: These are species that have a disproportionately large effect on their ecosystem relative to their abundance. The removal of a keystone species can drastically alter the ecosystem. For example, sea otters are a keystone species in kelp forests because they control the sea urchin population.

(d) Endemic species: These are species that are found only in one specific geographic location and nowhere else in the world. For example, the kangaroos of Australia or the lemurs of Madagascar are endemic to those regions.

Further insights

Pioneer species play a crucial role in primary succession, which occurs on newly formed land, such as bare rock after a volcanic eruption. Lichens are a classic example of a pioneer species in this context, as they can break down the rock and start the process of soil formation.

As you move from left to right across a period in the periodic table:

1. Protons are added: The number of protons in the nucleus increases by one for each successive element. This increases the overall positive charge of the nucleus (the nuclear charge).

2. Electrons are added to the same shell: The electrons being added are placed in the same principal energy level or electron shell.

3. Shielding is relatively constant: The number of inner-shell electrons, which are responsible for shielding the outer electrons from the full pull of the nucleus, remains the same. The electrons in the same outer shell do not shield each other effectively.

The combination of a stronger positive pull from the increasing number of protons and a relatively constant shielding effect from the inner electrons means that the effective nuclear charge-the net positive charge experienced by an outer-shell electron-increases. This stronger electrostatic attraction pulls the entire electron cloud closer to the nucleus, resulting in a smaller atomic radius.

Why the other options are incorrect:

(a) Increase in shielding effect: This is incorrect. The shielding effect does not increase significantly across a period because no new inner electron shells are added. An increase in shielding is the primary reason for the increase in atomic radius down a group.

(c) Decrease in nuclear charge: This is incorrect. The nuclear charge (the number of protons) steadily increases across a period.

(d) Addition of a new electron shell: This is incorrect. A new electron shell is added when moving down a group, which is why atomic radius increases down a group. Across a period, electrons fill the same outermost shell.

Further Insights:

This trend explains why an element like Fluorine (F) on the right side of Period 2 is much smaller than Lithium (Li) on the left side of the same period.

The concept of effective nuclear charge is crucial for explaining many periodic trends, including ionization energy and electronegativity, which also generally increase across a period due to the stronger pull of the nucleus on the electrons.

A transformer is a device that transfers electrical energy from one alternating-current (AC) circuit to another, either stepping up or stepping down the voltage. Its operation is based entirely on the principles of electromagnetic induction.

How it works:

Primary Coil: When an alternating current (AC) flows through the primary coil, it creates a continuously changing magnetic flux in the iron core.

Magnetic Core: The soft iron core concentrates and guides this changing magnetic flux, linking it to the secondary coil.

Secondary Coil: According to Faraday's Law of Induction, this changing magnetic flux induces an alternating electromotive force (EMF), or voltage, in the secondary coil.

Energy Transfer: This induced voltage in the secondary coil drives a current, thus transferring electrical energy from the primary circuit to the secondary circuit.

The key point is that the primary and secondary coils are electrically isolated from each other; there is no direct electrical connection between them. The energy transfer happens entirely through the medium of the magnetic field.
